name: Tauroursodeoxycholic acid (TUDCA)
short: In an ALS registry study, 8.1% of TUDCA users stopped it for mostly mild gut side effects and 2 adverse events needed hospital care. Small trials found adverse events similar to placebo or UDCA.
text: In a retrospective registry study in Italy, 86 people with amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) took TUDCA by mouth; it was generally well tolerated, but 7 (8.1%) stopped because of side effects, mainly gastrointestinal and mild, and 2 adverse events required hospital care and resolved without lasting effects. In a 16-week placebo-controlled trial in people with progressive multiple sclerosis (47 analysed), adverse events did not differ significantly between groups, and in a 24-week randomised trial in 199 Chinese patients with primary biliary cholangitis comparing TUDCA with ursodeoxycholic acid (UDCA, the related bile acid of which TUDCA is the taurine-conjugated form), both were well tolerated with comparable adverse event rates, while itching increased in the UDCA group but not in the TUDCA group. TUDCA has also been tested in ALS combined with sodium phenylbutyrate; in a 24-week randomised trial in 137 people with ALS of sodium phenylbutyrate-taurursodiol, adverse events with the active drug were mainly gastrointestinal, and the authors said longer and larger trials are needed to evaluate its safety. These studies are small or short, and the abstracts do not report long-term safety. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
